title: Language (Technology) is Power: A Critical Survey of “Bias” in NLP

bias_targets.methodology: A critical literature review and survey of 146 NLP papers, categorizing their evaluation techniques and motivations into allocational harms, representational harms (e.g., stereotyping), questionable correlations, and vague/unstated harms.

A detailed case study evaluating how existing NLP literature measures bias against African-American English (AAE), specifically analyzing system performance differences (e.g., part-of-speech taggers, dependency parsers) and disproportionate toxicity detection scores applied to AAE.

Reviewed and critiqued methodologies from surveyed papers, including evaluating gender stereotypes in word embeddings (e.g., WEAT), performance disparities in coreference resolution systems, and gender-neutral pronoun translation errors in machine translation.
